legend: Colorectal hamartomatous polyps - juvenile polyp.  These polyps contain plentiful lamina propria and cystically dilated glands.

In this large, multilobulated syndromic juvenile polyp, the surface shows erosion and granulation tissue. The epithelial compartment shows marked disarray and cystic change. The lamina propria also harbours a prominent smooth muscle component that is broad and haphazard, unlike a typical Peutz–Jeghers polyp.

Small juvenile polyps, even when syndromic, are morphologically indistinguishable from a sporadic one. The polyp here shows an expanded lamina propria with inflammation and slight crypt disarray. The patient had a known germline SMAD4 mutation.
